paragraphs: Hindus believe God has come to earth many times in different forms. When He came as Rama, His greatest devotee was Hanuman, who was also a mighty yogi and lived for a very long time.

Hanuman was still alive when Rama came again, this time as Krishna. Being a yogi, Hanuman recognised at once that it was the same God in a new form. He went to Krishna and served Him faithfully. But he had one request: he wanted to see Krishna in His Rama form.

Krishna asked whether this form was not good enough. He was Krishna and He was Rama; all these forms were His. Hanuman agreed completely. The Lord of Sita and the Lord of Lakshmi were the same Supreme Self, he said. And yet, for him, lotus-eyed Rama was everything.

Swamiji called this Nishtha: accepting that every form of worship is true, while holding firmly to your own. You do not have to worship the other forms, but you must never hate or mock them. You respect them, and you stay loyal to your own ideal.
learn: You can respect every path and still be fully committed to yours. Focus is not the same as narrow-mindedness. Pick your ideal, give it your heart, and let others do the same without needing them to be wrong.
